paper_info.title: Attention Is All You Need
paper_info.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.

presentation_flow.background_context: Sequence transduction models are crucial in tasks like language modeling and machine translation. Traditional models rely on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which are computationally intensive and less parallelizable. Attention mechanisms have emerged as a powerful tool to model dependencies in sequences, allowing for more efficient computation.
presentation_flow.problem_motivation: Existing state-of-the-art models, which use RNNs and CNNs, face limitations in parallelization due to their sequential nature. This results in longer training times and increased computational costs, especially for long sequences. The need for a more efficient model that can handle long-range dependencies without these constraints is evident.
presentation_flow.solution_overview: The Transformer model is introduced as a novel architecture that relies entirely on attention mechanisms, eliminating the need for recurrence and convolution. This design allows for greater parallelization and efficiency, achieving superior performance in machine translation tasks with reduced training time and computational resources.
presentation_flow.technical_approach: The Transformer architecture consists of an encoder-decoder structure using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers. Key components include multi-head attention, scaled dot-product attention, and position-wise feed-forward networks. Positional encodings are used to inject sequence order information.
presentation_flow.evidence_proof: Experiments on the WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks demonstrate the Transformer's superior performance, achieving BLEU scores of 28.4 and 41.8, respectively. These results surpass previous models, including ensembles, with significantly lower training costs.
presentation_flow.impact_significance: The Transformer sets a new standard in sequence transduction, offering faster training and improved performance. Future work includes extending the model to other modalities and exploring local attention mechanisms for handling large inputs like images and audio.

figures.caption: (left) Scaled Dot-Product Attention. (right) Multi-Head Attention consists of several attention layers running in parallel.
figures.analysis: The figure shows the mechanisms of scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention, which are key components of the Transformer's architecture.

figures.caption: An example of the attention mechanism following long-distance dependencies in the encoder self-attention in layer 5 of 6.
figures.analysis: This image demonstrates how the Transformer's attention mechanism can capture long-distance dependencies within a sequence, crucial for understanding context.

figures.caption: Two attention heads, also in layer 5 of 6, apparently involved in anaphora resolution.
figures.analysis: The figure illustrates the role of attention heads in resolving anaphora, showing the model's ability to track references within text.

figures.caption: Many of the attention heads exhibit behaviour that seems related to the structure of the sentence.
figures.analysis: This image highlights how different attention heads in the Transformer model learn to focus on various structural aspects of sentences.
